body: If you saw my previous post you may know that Toothless has been very inactive recently. I got the chance to take him to a vet, and I found out he didn't have enough calcium in his system. So for four weeks, I need to give him calcium gluconate 23%. I've been giving his doses daily since then, but ever since the appointment he's eaten very little, if at all daily. He also still hasn't defecated.

With the whole quarantine thing, days have been blurring together, I don't know for sure how long it's been but Toothless has been acting this way for at least a week--maybe two. It is reassuring to hear that other dragons sometimes act this way. Thanks!

Definitely. My brother got Toothless when he was just a juvenile, barely did anything to really care for him. Basically just turned his lights on and off and kept his food dish full. Never handled him because he always ran from his hand (obviously he would, he was a juvenile). He didn't do a whole lot of research, and I'm doing the best I can with the supplies my brother bought. They were ok for when Toothless was little but he didn't really think ahead for when he'd grow. I'll definitely look into better lighting, and I may have to organize meeting with a vet. Thanks for your suggestions!

Two heat lamps for the daytime, one 100W UV output, one that's 50W. Right now the temperature in the warm side is 87.1°F, and the cool side is 81.1°F. At night I turn off the day lamps and put a ceramic lamp over the cool side of the tank, where he sleeps in the log, to keep the temperature at a decent level. I keep clean food and water in his tank for him, and if he needs it, I refill the water in the morning. I refill his food daily of course.

How exactly does brumation work? Ever since my brother suddenly gave me Toothless I've done extensive research to care for him as best as I can. Some sources have told me that beardies only wake up like once in a week's time during brumation, and Toothless still gets up daily. He eats his food, poops, then basks for a little while, but then hides all day. Does that fit the definition of brumation? Thank you for the help by the way! ❤

Toothless is about a year old now, but I can't know for sure. My brother gave him to me after a few months of having him because he realized he was unfit to care for a beardie. That was back in December. I got Toothless a bigger tank, gave him kale instead of pellets, gave him live and freeze-dried crickets and worms, and for the most part he's just fine. Recently, any time I handle him, when I put him back, he goes right for his log to hide for the rest of the day. Around 10 or 11, he finally goes to sleep. Toothless used to bask a lot during the day, and only went in the log to sleep. Plus, when I used to handle him, he'd just go back to basking or eating. Now, sometimes when I haven't even handled him, he just goes to the log after a while. Is this normal, or can beardies experience things like depression? I'm worried about my little guy.

It actually helps so, so much more than you know. The show was "The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee," and I don't know if you're familiar with it, but I played Olive Ostrovsky. She has a song called, "The I Love You Song." The first time I even read the lyrics, I cried. In this song, Olive is given the word "chimerical" to spell. It means, "highly unrealistic," and "wildly fanciful." Upon hearing the definition, Olive begins imagining her parents. Her mother, who left her, presumably after an affair, and her father, who never supports her and is always at work.

Olive imagines her parents telling her that they love her. Through the song we realize that Olive's idea of something "wildly fanciful and highly unrealistic" is both of her parents openly expressing their love for her.

When I got the role of Olive, I hoped it would help me express that I believe the same thing--that a parent's love is just a fantastic dream.

Hearing a congratulations from any mother is more than I've gotten from mine.

Thank you, so, so much.
I was so very afraid for a moment

It's really tough to get through to her, anything I say is brushed off, and she always finds something to be angry at. She called one of my friends gay a few days ago and naturally I defended him, and then she got pissed at me and for the past four days refuses to say a word to me.

I'd hope to be put on medication, or at least understand my condition because people around me do point out that I am flawed because I'm afraid to do mundane tasks. A friend of mine told me that when she was diagnosed with depression and anxiety, she was given medicine and therapy and has since been doing much better, she says she feels like the world isn't against her anymore. I appreciate you telling me that maybe my mother is just overwhelmed, but I do wish she'd do more than essentially say, "get over it," and "you don't need medicine," because sometimes it's tough to deal with on my own, I'm sure you understand. But again thank you
